ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening under FINTRAC requirements: identify and verify every individual who owns or controls 25% or more of the entity; screen against federal PEP lists, Global Affairs Canada sanctions under the Special Economic Measures Act and United Nations Act, the OSFI consolidated sanctions list, UN Security Council consolidated list, and for USD transactions OFAC SDN list; document screening at client onboarding and on any material change; maintain enhanced due diligence where the entity or its clients are politically exposed persons or from high-risk jurisdictions.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec online services (Services en ligne) — registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca; for federal name reservation: Corporations Canada online Name Reservation Request — ised-isde.canada.ca
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Quebec corporate names must include a French version; the French version is the official name for exercise of civil rights in Quebec and must be used in judicial and extrajudicial documents unless an exception applies. Non-French names may be used together with an equally prominent French version, subject to the Charter of the French Language (CQLR c C-11). Federal names may be in English, French, or both; if bilingual, the English and French forms must be equivalent and the name must not create confusion with existing names.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: For Quebec, if the Registraire refuses a name, the applicant may file a new reservation or submit formal written representations addressed to the Direction de l'évaluation des noms within 30 days of the refusal, citing the legal basis and evidence of distinctiveness; in case of a second refusal, an administrative review may be sought before the Administrative Tribunal of Quebec. For a federal name refusal, the applicant may file a written request for reconsideration with the Director General of Corporations Canada within 90 days of the refusal, providing submissions, trademark evidence and consents, and may thereafter seek judicial review in the Federal Court within 30 days of the reconsideration decision.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Yes, a virtual office is permissible for a low-risk professional services corporation provided the registered office is a physical location in Quebec (or Canada for federal incorporation) where legal process can be served, and not solely a post office box; a commercial virtual office with mail collection, business address and process-agent facilities is acceptable, but the corporation must maintain real books, records, corporate registers and decision-making substance for tax residency and GST/QST registration.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate: approximately 10–15% probability over the first three years of operation; the risk rises to 25–40% if the registered office address is used by numerous unrelated companies, if tax filings show no employees, or if banking/AML alerts identify the corporation as a shell risk.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Quebec Business Corporations Act (Loi sur les sociétés par actions), CQLR c S-31.1, ss. 5-18 (incorporation and articles), ss. 23-25 (certificate of incorporation), ss. 31-33 (registered office and records), ss. 103-116 (directors), ss. 189-201 (officers); and the Legal Publicity of Enterprises Act (Loi sur la publicité légale des entreprises), CQLR c P-44.1, ss. 2-10.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ), 2050, rue Bleury, Montréal, Québec H3A 2H5; online portal: Registraire des entreprises en ligne (registraire.gouv.qc.ca).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Statuts constitutifs), filed electronically through the Registraire des entreprises en ligne; the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation (Attestation de constitution) and the Quebec enterprise number (NEQ).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under the QBCA; the corporation may be capitalized with nominal share consideration determined by the board. No escrow account or capital deposit requirement applies; the former CAD 10,000 minimum was repealed.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: BE IT RESOLVED THAT: 1. The incorporation of the Corporation under the Quebec Business Corporations Act, CQLR c S-31.1, and the registration of its Articles of Incorporation with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec are hereby ratified and confirmed. 2. The subscription and allotment of 100 common shares to the founding subscriber, in consideration of the contribution approved by the board, are approved. 3. The registered office of the Corporation is established at [street address, city], Province of Quebec. 4. The preliminary by-laws are adopted, effective immediately, until ratified by the shareholders. 5. [Name] is appointed President, [Name] Secretary, and [Name] Treasurer (Chief Financial Officer); each officer shall serve until the next annual general meeting, with full authority to execute banking and statutory filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Quebec Corporate Name Declaration and NUANS Search
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Contrôleur des renseignements relatifs aux noms via the Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) and an accredited NUANS search house
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain a NUANS/Preliminary Research Report for the proposed French or bilingual corporate name; validate that the name is distinct and does not conflict with trademarks, legal persons, or enterprise names registered in Quebec; file the declaration of name (déclaration de nom) with REQ or incorporate directly using the reserved name.
required_dossiers: NUANS preliminary research report (validity 90 days)
Declaration of name form (if filed separately)
Written authorization from the proposed incorporator or shareholder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or queried, submit an amended declaration with up to two alternative distinctive names within the original registration window; no additional statutory fee applies for the first alternative name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Articles of Incorporation and Issuance of the Attestation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) - online filing service (Registraire des entreprises en ligne)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare and sign the Articles of Incorporation (Statuts constitutifs) in French, stating the corporate name, share structure with classes and attached rights, restrictions on share transfers or business activities (if any), the number of directors, the initial registered office address in Quebec (a real street address, not a post office box), and the mandate of the directors; submit electronically, pay the statutory fee, and receive the Attestation de constitution and NEQ number.
required_dossiers: Articles of Incorporation (Statuts constitutifs) duly signed by the incorporator
Declaration of name confirmation (if applicable)
Evidence of payment of the CAD 322 filing fee
Identity documents of each director and officer
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a notice of query or refusal, correct the inconsistencies in the online draft and resubmit within 30 days; the original registration date is preserved when the correction does not alter essential elements.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organizational Formalities: First Board Resolution, By-laws and Share Subscription
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the Corporation (internal corporate governance)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the inaugural board meeting or adopt a unanimous written resolution to ratify incorporation, approve the allotment of shares to the founding subscriber, establish the registered office, appoint officers, adopt preliminary by-laws, and open the corporate records book and securities register; authorize opening bank accounts and executing banking mandates.
required_dossiers: Pro-forma first board resolution
Minutes of the organizational meeting or written consent in lieu of meeting
By-laws No. 1 of the Corporation
Registered office notification and consent of the occupant
Share subscription agreement and securities register
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: N/A (internal step); any omitted officer appointment or by-law item is ratified by an additional written consent in lieu of meeting signed by all directors.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Quebec Tax Registration with Revenu Québec (QST, Payroll and NEQ)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Revenu Québec - online business portal (Mon dossier entreprise)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the Corporation for the Quebec Sales Tax (TVQ/QST) under the Act respecting the Quebec Sales Tax (CQLR c T-0.1) when taxable supplies exceed the CAD 30,000 threshold; open the employer payroll account for source deductions, contributions to the Québec parental insurance plan (QPIP), and the health services fund (FSS); confirm that all NEQ registry data, including the chief place of business and director information, is current.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation (Attestation de constitution)
NEQ (Quebec enterprise number) confirmation
Business address and list of directors and officers
Corporate bank account details and contact information
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registration is queried or placed in abeyance, provide the missing supporting documents and a signed authorization letter via Mon dossier entreprise; Revenu Québec will backdate the account effective date upon cure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal Registration with the Canada Revenue Agency (GST/HST, Payroll and Corporate Income Tax)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) - Business Registration Online (BRO)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Create the CRA business number (BN) account for the Corporation; register for the GST/HST account under the Excise Tax Act (R.S.C. 1985, c. E-15) if worldwide taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000; open the payroll deductions account (RP) for income tax, CPP and EI; confirm the corporate income tax account and select the fiscal year-end (e.g., December 31) and filing obligations.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation (Attestation de constitution)
NEQ confirmation from the Registraire des entreprises du Québec
Registered office address in Canada
Estimated annual revenue, fiscal year-end, and bank account details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CRA queries the registration, provide the certificate of corporate status and reconfirm the business number through the Represent a Client channel; the CRA generally activates or reinstates the accounts within 5 business days after verification.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) for activity registration; Ville de Montréal / local municipal authority for the commercial establishment permit; Ordre des comptables professionnels agréés du Québec (CPA Order) for reserved public accounting acts.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Commercial Establishment Operating Permit (Permis d'exploitation d'un établissement commercial) issued by the competent municipal authority; additionally, a CPA Firm Permit (Permis de société de comptables professionnels agréés) is mandatory only if the Corporation performs reserved acts such as certification of financial statements.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category C - Exempt from the environmental impact assessment procedure (service activity); the outsourced virtual CFO office does not meet any Schedule I threshold of the Regulation respecting the environmental impact assessment of projects (REAFIE). A full EIA is not required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No point-source industrial discharges; office operations must comply with municipal wastewater by-laws and the Regulation respecting municipal wastewater treatment works; zero VOC-emitting processes; waste electrical and electronic equipment must be recovered by a registered producer under the Electronics Products Recovery and Recycling Regulation (Recyc-Québec).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Certificate of fire safety (attestation de sécurité incendie) issued by the local fire safety service under the Fire Safety Act; compliance with the Quebec Building Code structural and occupant load requirements; CNESST occupational health clearance under the Act respecting occupational health and safety (CQLR c S-2.1) covering electrical, ergonomic and telework workstation conditions; municipal home-occupation permit where the head office is operated from a residential unit.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency / Agence du revenu du Canada (CRA) — federal GST/HST and Part I corporate income tax; secure portal: CRA My Business Account (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services/cra-login-services/business-account.html); business registration: Business Registration Online (https://www.canada.ca/business-registration). Revenu Québec / Agence du revenu du Québec — Quebec Sales Tax (QST), Quebec corporate income tax and source deductions; secure portal: CLIC (https://www.revenuquebec.ca/en/online-services/l-clic/). Non-tax corporate registry in Quebec: Registraire des entreprises (https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca).

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada); exchange-rate policy is coordinated with the Department of Finance Canada, and cross-border financial-transaction reporting is administered by FINTRAC. Canada has no standalone foreign-exchange control authority requiring transaction-level FX permits.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is fully convertible for both current and capital account purposes. There is no foreign-exchange licensing, surrender, or prior-approval requirement for treasury payments, shareholder capital injections, procurement disbursements, or profit repatriation. Inbound foreign investment may be subject to review under the Investment Canada Act only when the transaction involves acquisition of control of a Canadian business above statutory thresholds. Profit remittance is tax-driven rather than FX-driven: dividends, interest, royalties, and certain management fees paid to non-residents are subject to Part XIII withholding tax under the Income Tax Act, generally 25% statutory, reduced under applicable tax treaties, with Quebec parallel rules under the Tax Administration Act where relevant. In addition, Quebec corporate law solvency tests must be satisfied before any dividend or capital distribution.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender requirement, no mandatory conversion timeline, and no required conversion ratio apply to export receipts in Canada. Exporters may hold foreign currency in Canadian bank accounts without conversion. Obligations are limited to tax and trade reporting: export declarations and customs documentation through the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA), corporate income tax and Quebec tax filings, GST/QST and customs compliance, and FINTRAC reporting by financial institutions for international electronic funds transfers of C$10,000 or more.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: National Bank of Canada / Banque Nationale du Canada
Laurentian Bank of Canada / Banque Laurentienne du Canada

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium-High as a payment adjunct, Low as a standalone clearing or escrow rail. Foreign digital EMIs such as Wise are not chartered banks under the Bank Act, are not members of Payments Canada, and cannot issue Canadian demand-deposit instruments, commercial letters of credit, or provide CDIC-insured balances. They may operate as FINTRAC-registered money services businesses (MSBs) and, when fully licensed, support payment routing such as Stripe billing or Wise payouts, but funds must be backed by a regulated Canadian Schedule I bank account for statutory treasury operations, CRA remittances, payroll, and FX clearing. A Quebec business corporation should use such platforms solely as software-enabled payment conduits, never as the primary account holder of corporate liquidity.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote account opening is permitted under Canadian AML/CFT law, but physical presence becomes a de facto mandate for fully virtual, non-resident, or newly incorporated companies. FINTRAC customer due diligence requires identification of all directors, signing officers, and beneficial owners owning 25% or more of the corporation. Most major Canadian banks will not open an account remotely for a virtual CFO entity without one of the following: a notarized certificate of incumbency, valid government-issued identification for each controller, a Canadian business address and registered-office document, and at least one in-person interview with the primary authorized signatory or a Canada-based director. A remote-only opening can be accepted by select banks through enhanced video verification with notarized/certified copies, but this is discretionary, never a statutory right.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Offshore corporate layers and beneficial-ownership chain involving non-Canadian LLCs, trusts, or foreign holding companies
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete FINTRAC UBO register listing all direct/indirect owners above 25%; copy of each underlying entity's corporate registry extract; trust deed or declaration of trust where applicable; notarized organizational chart; passports and tax identification numbers of all controllers; share certificates; board resolutions approving the banking mandate; notarized certificate of incumbency; source-of-wealth letter from the foreign holding entity's regulated bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Virtual-only operations with no physical office or no verifiable Canadian substance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Quebec head-office address and proof of registered office under the Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ); signed lease or virtual-office service agreement with physical mail-handling evidence; client contracts for fractional CFO advisory services; board minutes; service-delivery ledgers; vendor invoices and expense trail; utility/telecom bills; annual financial statements; notarized declaration of Canadian substance for AML purposes.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Politically exposed persons (PEPs) or adverse media match among directors/shareholders
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent PEP and sanctions screening results for every controller and signatory; source of funds and source of wealth report; certified bank reference letters; professional references from accountants or law firms; explanation of commercial purpose; evidence that business funds are unrelated to public-office assets; audit trail of all anticipated inbound and outbound flows.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual multicurrency ledger, frequent cross-border wires, and low domestic payroll for a virtual CFO operation
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Expected transaction profile and monthly wire forecast; executed client engagement letters describing CFO and bookkeeping services; per-wire purpose mapping to invoices; chart of accounts and accounting ledger; complete audit trail for multicurrency balance sheets; internal AML transaction-monitoring policy; evidence of how Stripe billing and Wise rail balances will be swept to the Canadian bank account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of funds involving crypto exchanges, high-risk fintech corridors, or unsupported digital-value transfers
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank-sourced receipt from a regulated financial institution, not directly from crypto custody; serialized fiat withdrawal/completion records; cryptocurrency-to-fiat statements where applicable; client invoices referencing the exact payment; source-of-wealth letter; external accountant's confirmation of capitalization; board resolution authorizing the funding method.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-arm's-length shareholder loans without clear commercial rationale or repayment documentation
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed shareholder loan agreements; promissory notes; interest-rate analysis; IFRS or ASPE capitalization memo; solvency analysis; detailed repayment schedule; board resolutions; financial statements reflecting the loans as intercompany receivables/payables; tax analysis confirming Part XIII withholding or Part I transfer-pricing treatment as applicable.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Foreign-parent equity injections and shareholder loans must be routed by SWIFT MT103 or high-value telegraphic transfer to the corporation's Canadian bank account, with beneficiary field referencing the Quebec business corporation and account number; CAD settlement occurs through Payments Canada Lynx for high-value transactions. Bank correspondence must include the remittance purpose in the SWIFT field 70 narrative, for example 'Capital contribution', 'Shareholder loan', or 'Service fee under contract', together with invoice or board-resolution references. No exchange-control permit is required, but the bank will verify the source via supporting documents: share subscription agreement, board resolution, loan agreement, and beneficial-owner identification. For amounts equal to or exceeding C$10,000, the financial institution files a FINTRAC international electronic funds-transfer report; the corporation must maintain documentary proof of the underlying transaction for CRA, Quebec tax, and banking compliance.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Cross-border outbound payments from the Quebec corporation clear via SWIFT MT103 or MT202 COVER through the corporate bank's correspondent network; CAD disbursements settle on Payments Canada Lynx rail. For documentary trade settlements, an irrevocable Commercial Letter of Credit is opened under UCP600 via MT700, with standby letters of credit under ISP98 where required. Supplier payments for virtual CFO subcontracting, software licenses, and multicurrency ledger platforms can use direct wire transfer with invoice support and purpose-code narrative; USD and foreign-currency payments may be cleared through a U.S. correspondent, SWIFT GPI, or the bank's in-house multicurrency treasury desk. For high-frequency low-value payouts, ACH and card rails are acceptable only when swept to a funded operating account; they do not replace bank wire for treasury-critical transactions.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Spot CAD/FX contracts for immediate conversion of foreign-currency inflows and outflows
Deliverable CAD FX outright forwards, normally up to 12 months, for hedging known invoicing and receivables exposure
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for settlement in non-convertible or restricted currencies where cash settlement in CAD is required
Cross-currency swaps between CAD and USD/EUR for maturity-matched capital structure hedging
FX options, vanilla puts/calls, and zero-cost collars for downside protection without upside restriction
ISDA-documented trades under a bank derivative master agreement, subject to Canadian derivative conduct rules under National Instrument 93-101 and applicable Quebec securities regulation

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due annually within 60 days after the anniversary date of enterprise registration in the Registraire des entreprises du Québec; the registraire issues reminder notices before the due date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers successive administrative reminders and penalty charges under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises; continued non-filing for two consecutive anniversary cycles leads to administrative strike-off or dissolution of the corporation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Annual Return (when the entity is formed or continued under the Canada Business Corporations Act)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Director appointed under the Canada Business Corporations Act / Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due annually within 60 days after the anniversary date of incorporation or amalgamation, in addition to the Quebec jurisdictional filing.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or omitted filing may lead to a notice of default and, after two consecutive years of failure, administrative dissolution under section 261 of the CBCA; directors may also be subject to offence-related penalties.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory audit is compulsory for reporting issuers, banks, insurance, trust and loan companies, and other federally governed financial institutions. A non-distributing private corporation is not required to appoint an auditor if all shareholders resolve unanimously, in writing, to dispense with an auditor for the relevant fiscal year; absent such waiver the shareholders must appoint an auditor, and any shareholder may also compel an audit by requisition.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Financial statements must be prepared in accordance with the CPA Canada Handbook: IFRS for public/reporting issuers and, at the election of the entity, IFRS or Canadian ASPE for private corporations; for the subject virtual-CFO services business, ASPE is the customary framework.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: At each anniversary cycle, the corporation must verify that the shareholder register reflects all transfers occurring during the preceding year and confirm the identity of every individual with significant control (generally any individual holding 25% or more of votes or value). For CBCA corporations, changes to significant-control information must be recorded in the Register of Individuals with Significant Control and updated in the annual return; for Quebec provincial corporations, the annual declaration must re-affirm the same significant-control data. A notice of any share transfer that changes significant control must also be recorded in the register within 15 days of becoming known to the corporation.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Combined federal and Quebec general corporate rate 26.5% (federal 15% after the general rate reduction; Quebec 11.5%); CCPC small business rate 12.2% on first CAD 500,000 of active business income (federal 9% + Quebec 3.2%)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Federal Small Business Deduction (SBD) reduces federal rate from 28% to 9% on the CAD 500,000 business limit; Quebec reduced rate of 3.2% on the first CAD 500,000 of eligible CCPC active business income; refundable SR&ED investment tax credit of 35% for CCPCs on qualified expenditures up to CAD 3,000,000; Quebec SR&ED refundable credit (30% for SMEs, 14% for large); Quebec digitalization tax credit (refundable up to 25% of eligible expenses) applicable to the virtual CFO firm's own technology adoption

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return — Canada Revenue Agency (CRA); mandatory electronic E-file via certified tax software (e.g., IntelliForm, CanTax) through the EFILE system or CRA 'My Business Account'; XML schema 'T2' transmitted by an authorized E-file service provider; due regardless of nil taxable income
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing deadline: six (6) months after fiscal year-end. Balance-due date: two (2) months after fiscal year-end for most corporations; three (3) months for an eligible CCPC claiming the SBD on active business income. U.S.-domiciled non-resident corporations filing on a non-calendar year must align Canadian fiscal period to treaty-adjusted reporting.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: CRA-issued 9-digit business number with program account 'RC0001'
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident corporation carrying on business in Canada through a permanent establishment must register for a BN via Form RC148 and enter the PE-establishing Canadian address

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T2 page 1 – Fiscal year-end / legal name / jurisdiction of incorporation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Entity identification block used by CRA to match registration records
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter foreign jurisdiction of incorporation (e.g., Delaware or British Columbia for U.S. parent structures) and Canadian branch/PE address; attach a copy of the Certificate of Corporate Status

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income as computed under section 3 of the Income Tax Act (ITA), after reserves, deductions, and non-capital loss carryovers
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident corporation subject to Part I tax on Canadian-source business income under ITA s.2(3), compute only the income attributable to the Canadian permanent establishment in accordance with the PE profit attribution rules

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deduction reducing federal tax to 9% on active business income up to the CAD 500,000 business limit (subject to associated-corporate rules and passive income grind)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Available only to Canadian-controlled private corporations (CCPC); a U.S.-parented Canadian corporation generally does not qualify unless operating through a newly incorporated CCPC before ownership is transferred to non-residents

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: 13% reduction on taxable income not eligible for the SBD, bringing the general federal rate to 15%
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Applies to all corporations resident in Canada, including foreign-controlled subsidiaries taxed on worldwide income; a non-resident branch (Part I taxpayer) is not entitled to this relief

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregate federal income tax after SBD, GRR, investment tax credits, and foreign tax credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Part I tax computed on the T2; installments are due in four quarterly installments based on the prior-year estimate; interest accrues daily and penalties attach for non-payment

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: 5% of unpaid balance plus 1% per full month of delay (max 12 months); repeated failure within 3 years adds 10% + 2% per month (max 20 months); nil-balance late filing fixed penalty CAD 100 (ITA s.162(1)); gross negligence penalty 50% of understated federal tax (ITA s.163(2)); daily compound interest at prescribed rates (CRA prescribed rate + up to 6% for large corporations) from the balance-due date; unreported foreign-source income of the Canadian subsidiary exposes the shareholder to Part XIII reassessment

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: CO-17 Corporation Income Tax Return — Revenu Québec; electronic filing via 'Mon dossier d'affaires' (Business Account) or Revenu Québec-certified software; mandatory e-transmission for tax years ending on or after a date set by Revenu Québec (all corporations are effectively required to file electronically)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (same fiscal period as the federal T2)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing deadline: six (6) months after fiscal year-end. Balance-due date: two (2) months after year-end; three (3) months for eligible CCPCs. Québec's collection agreement with CRA aligns the payment dates but does not alter the CO-17 filing requirement.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Revenu Québec enterprise number (NEQ) and the federal BN; business sector code ISIC 6920 / NAICS 541219
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident corporation with a Quebec (PE) must obtain a Quebec establishment number and register for the QST/GST via the 'Business Registration' portal and enter the PE address in Quebec

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: CO-17 Part II – Line 100 'Revenu imposable' (taxable income)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income aligned with the federal T2 Schedule 1 line 460 with Quebec-specific reconciliation adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the Quebec PE income allocation under the Taxation Act; transactions with the foreign head office must be documented under Quebec's transfer-pricing rules mirroring ITA s.247

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: CO-17 Part II – Line 200 'Impôt avant crédits' (tax before credits)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Provincial tax computed at 11.5% general rate or 3.2% reduced SME rate on the first CAD 500,000 of eligible active business income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The reduced rate requires CCPC status and a permanent establishment in Quebec; a foreign-controlled subsidiary may claim the reduced rate only if it meets the 90% Canadian-resident shareholder test

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: CO-17 Part II – Line 300 'Crédits d'impôt' (tax credits)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Refundable and non-refundable Quebec credits, including SR&ED, digitalization, and tax havens prevention credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents may claim only credits for activities physically carried on in Quebec; the SR&ED credit requires that the salary and expenditures be paid through a Quebec payroll account

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: CO-17 Part II – Line 400 'Solde dû ou remboursement' (balance due or refund)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net provincial tax liability after installment payments and credit carryovers
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Instalments must be remitted to Revenu Québec; a non-resident corporation without a Quebec payroll is still liable for daily compound interest from the statutory due date

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Revenu Québec late-filing penalty: 5% of the unpaid balance plus 1% per full month (max 12 months); repeated failure: 10% + 2% per month (max 24 months); refusal or omission to provide information: CAD 1,000–CAD 25,000; false statements or omissions (gross negligence): 50% of the understated provincial tax; daily compound interest at Revenu Québec's prescribed rate (federal base rate + 4%); unpaid CO-17 balances are registered as hypothecs (provincial liens) on the corporation's property

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% federal Part XIII on all dividends paid or credited (ITA s.212(2)); no separate Quebec dividend withholding tax. Reduced to 5% under the Canada–U.S. treaty for a corporate resident of the United States that beneficially owns at least 10% of the voting shares; 15% in all other treaty cases. Under the Canada–China DTA, dividend withholding is reduced to 10% (or 5% for a 10%+ corporate shareholder).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The Canadian payer must apply the reduced treaty rate at source only where it has reasonable grounds. Protocol: (1) obtain the non-resident beneficial owner's completed Form NR301 (Declaration of Eligibility for Benefits Under a Tax Treaty; use NR302/NR303 for hybrid or partnership/REIT structures); (2) obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the foreign tax authority, e.g., IRS Form 6166 or a Chinese State Taxation Administration 'Certificate of Resident Status'; (3) for US payees, obtain a valid Form W-8BEN-E with U.S. TIN; (4) retain the documentation in the Canadian payer's books for review; (5) do not file for a refund via Form NR7-R (which is used only if withholding was applied in excess). Failure to support the treaty rate renders the Canadian payer liable for the unwithheld 25% under ITA s.215 plus interest and penalties.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Part XIII rates: 25% on royalties (use or right to use any copyright, patent, trademark, secret process, or know-how — ITA s.212(1)(d)) and 25% on interest (ITA s.212(1)(b)). Canada–U.S. treaty: interest 0% on arm's-length interest and 15% on non-arm's length; royalties 0% for copyright and software licensing, 10% for industrial royalties (patents, trademarks, know-how). Canada–China DTA: interest 10%, royalties 10%. Quebec does not impose a separate WHT on cross-border royalties or interest.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No statutory dollar safe harbor for contemporaneous documentation. Mandatory Form T106 'Information Return of Non-Arm's Length Transactions with Non-Residents' where the aggregate fair market value of reportable transactions in a taxation year exceeds CAD 1,000,000; Country-by-Country Report (CbCR) mandatory for MNE groups with annual consolidated revenue of at least CAD 750,000,000 (OECD BEPS Action 13). Canada has not enacted a separate Master File/Local File statutory threshold, but CRA transfer-pricing review letters request the OECD-aligned documentation and penalties apply under ITA s.247(3).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Offshore-style Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) do not apply in Canada. Canadian residency follows 'central management and control' (ITA s.250); a Quebec-incorporated virtual CFO corporation is resident in Canada and subject to worldwide taxation. The CRA attacks artificial 'letter-box' companies through the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR, ITA s.245) and Quebec's parallel GAAR in the Taxation Act; excessive management fees, back-to-back royalty arrangements, and intercompany invoicing without real employees or premises in Quebec are recharacterized. A pure tax-residency certificate without operational substance in Quebec does not protect against CRA reassessment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends, interest, or royalties to a non-resident parent or shareholder at the reduced treaty rate without the required TRC and treaty declaration, or routing payments through a zero-WHT conduit without economic substance; failing to withhold 25% at source
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ITA s.215: the Canadian payer is jointly and severally liable for the entire unwithheld Part XIII amount, plus daily compound interest and penalties; gross negligence penalties of 50% of the unremitted amount under ITA s.163(2); CRA may waive the treaty reduction back and assess the 25% rate for up to three years of amendments plus a further three under the Part XIII omission rules
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the Canadian payer are personally, jointly, and severally liable for unremitted Part XIII amounts (ITA s.227.1) even after the corporation is dissolved; criminal prosecution under ITA s.242 for willful evasion carries imprisonment up to five (5) years; non-resident directors convicted of tax fraud become inadmissible to Canada under IRPA s.36(1)(c) and subject to removal and travel bans

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Mispricing / Management Fee Shifting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging inflated 'management fees' or 'virtual CFO royalties' to the Canadian operating subsidiary without staff, premises, or functional risk in the foreign parent; failing to file Form T106 for non-arm's length transactions above CAD 1,000,000; producing no comparability analysis for the intercompany pricing of bookkeeping and advisory services
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ITA s.247(2) permits the CRA to recharacterize non-arm's length transactions to the arm's length price; s.247(3) imposes a 10% penalty on the net adjustment where the adjustment exceeds the lesser of CAD 5,000,000 or 10% of the taxpayer's gross revenue; Quebec reassessment follows the federal transfer pricing adjustment automatically; interest accrues from the original due date
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly signed false T106 schedules or who materially misrepresented the intercompany pricing face gross negligence penalties under ITA s.163.2 (preparer/planner penalty of CAD 1,000 to CAD 100,000 plus 100% of the planning fees); the CRA's 'intermediary penalty' reaches CFO consultants, and convicted directors face imprisonment of up to two years; the penalties are not dischargeable in bankruptcy (BIA s.178(1)(a))

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: GAAR Abuse / Shell Company Substance Deficiency
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Incorporating a Quebec 'letter-box' corporation that invoices virtual CFO services to U.S. clients but books the profit in a zero-tax jurisdiction through a back-to-back licensing or 'cost-plus' arrangement with no employees, no office, and no board meetings with real decision-making in Quebec
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR (ITA s.245) nullifies the tax benefit and the CRA re-prices the full profit to Canada; as amended by the 2024 legislation, a special 50% penalty applies on the GAAR benefit for transactions entered into after June 12, 2024, in addition to the reassessed tax and daily compound interest; Quebec applies its own GAAR and can assess an additional 10% penalty for false declarations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and shareholders who caused the corporation to enter the abusive scheme are assessed personally for the 50% GAAR penalty to the extent they were 'participants' in the avoidance transaction; corporate veil is pierced for tax debts owed to the Crown; for non-resident directors, a finding of willful participation in tax evasion triggers inadmissibility to Canada and a travel ban, plus potential extradition for fraud over CAD 5,000 under the Criminal Code
